title: Carry the trace into the tool call
lesson: A tool that calls another service must propagate the trace context (the traceparent header) or the service's spans land in a separate trace and a failed agent task cannot be followed into the dependency that failed.
transcript: 0–8.35s: Task 7 calls charge() and receives 200 from the Billing API. The agent records invoke_agent and execute_tool under trace 4bf9; the service records POST /charge 200 under trace 91c0. Another caller adds trace a7e3. The task succeeds despite the missing trace connection.

8.35–17.56s: Task 8 receives a downstream 500. Its agent trace is c3a1, while the service failure is recorded under 0d12. A red dashed join appears at 13.85s, the service rows are scanned, and a question mark appears at 15.26s: none matches c3a1.
17.56–19.96s: The old agent trace clears. At 18.26s charge() gains + traceparent with a blue pulse, representing propagation configured for subsequent requests.

19.96–25.36s: New task 9 starts under trace 7e2d. A blue traceparent 7e2d chip crosses to the service around 22.01–22.56s. The API still returns 500; its new recorded span has trace 7e2d, matching the agent trace.

25.36–29.57s: A blue flowing dotted join routes to the matching 7e2d API row. Unrelated rows dim, the matching error row gains a blue selection outline while retaining its red failure status, and the question mark becomes a check. The linked failure holds until 28.56s, then the stage fades to the opening title card. Correlation is repaired; the API failure remains.
limitations: Illustrative scenario: three tasks, one tool and one service, with trace ids shortened to four hex characters; a real traceparent carries a 32-hex trace id and a 16-hex parent id, and a real backend holds many more spans.

Propagation also requires receiver extraction, instrumentation and recording/export to queryable telemetry storage; sampling or export failures can omit evidence. A common backend is convenient, not a requirement of the trace-context protocol. The header does not prevent the failure, change retries, or authorize the request.
Agent span names (invoke_agent, execute_tool) follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, which are marked Development and may change.
Audio was verified by analysis only (encoded peak -1.6 dBFS, spectrogram, cue timing against the scene); it was not listened to.
Originally self-reviewed by the author; subsequently compared and corrected in reviews/comparisons/observability-and-tracing/ with original provenance preserved.
Span operation labels are illustrative, not exact exported GenAI span names; matching shortened trace IDs show membership, while concrete parent/span IDs are omitted.

sources.title: Semantic conventions for GenAI agent and framework spans — OpenTelemetry

corrections.change: Replaced whole-history glow with a blue selection of only the matching 7e2d error row; routed the join to that row and dimmed unrelated history. Red error status is preserved.
Aligned transcript boundaries with the encoded sequence, including 17.56s reset, 18.26s propagation cue, 19.96s new task and 25.36s correlation. Corrected solid-line wording to flowing dotted join.
